newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin's daughters see improvement in his eyes.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin's daughters see improvement in his eyes.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin's daughters, clearly relieved their father's multiple heart bypass has gone well, said on Sunday they could see the improvement in his health in the Russian president's eyes.

"Every day he changes, he really looks better...even the expression in his eyes changes," Yelena told NTV commercial television in an interview at Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital, where she had just shared a meal with her 65-year-old father.
Sitting next to her younger sister, Tatyana, she said the pain was visible in Yeltsin's eyes in the days after the surgery. "Now if he is not happy with us, I wouldn't say he shouts, but..."
Doctors said on Sunday that Yeltsin was in "satisfactory condition" after Tuesday's seven-hour quintuple bypass operation but would stay in hospital for eight to 10 days.
His daughters said Yeltsin was already beginning to work on papers in his suite of rooms.
They said they had known the operation was necessary but had been confident it would be successful.
"We were very confident that all would be well because with Dad, everything always goes well," said Yelena.
At that, with a laugh, both women knocked on wood for luck.
Tatyana said their mother, Naina, spent most of every day in the hospital with her husband, leaving at about 8 p.m.
Yeltsin has yet to regain his appetite but Tatyana said it would return as he got around more.
Naina and his daughters were giving the clinic cooks advice on how to tempt him. But he touched little apart from a mouthful or two of pelmeni (Siberian ravioli).
Keen to get back to work, Yeltsin already has "a mountain of papers" on his desk at the clinic, but is not having meetings, or even watching the television in his room, they said.
Asked when Yeltsin would return to a full programme of work, Tatyana said: "It is better not to guess."
She said that, because of the stitches in his chest, coughing was painful for Yeltsin, and he was supposed to hold a pillow against his chest when he did.
A U.S. society of patients who have undergone open heart surgery had sent Yeltsin a warm letter of support -- and a small pillow with a red heart sewn on to it.
Tatyana, 36, played an active role in her father's re-election campaign earlier this year and some analysts have seen her as an influential figure behind the scenes.
Asked if she planned to continue in politics, she would say only: "It is difficult to say how things will be now. As Dad sees fit, I will always help in any capacity."
